title: DbContext: Unit of Work in EF Core

scenes.say: Ever wonder why DbContext is at the heart of Entity Framework Core? What does it actually do for you?

scenes.label: Pattern
scenes.sub: DbContext tracks changes and saves them as one transaction.
scenes.say: DbContext uses the unit of work pattern. It tracks every change you make and saves them all together in one go.

rows.b: Commit all changes in one transaction

scenes.say: You spin up a DbContext, make your changes, call SaveChanges, and then dispose it. That’s your workflow.
With tracking, DbContext spots changes and saves them. Without tracking, queries are faster but updates aren’t possible.

scenes.question: Should you reuse DbContext across requests?
scenes.right: No, it causes memory leaks and stale data. Use a new DbContext for each unit of work.
scenes.say: Don’t reuse DbContext across requests. That leads to memory leaks and stale data. Always start fresh for each unit of work.
